title: ICE Fatally Shoots Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston; Victim Was Not Operation Target
excerpt: An ICE agent shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, 52, a Mexican construction worker in Houston whose van agents mistook for one connected to their actual target. DHS alleged Salgado Araujo weaponized his vehicle; witnesses and family disputed that account, and agents were not wearing body cameras.
content:
On July 7, 2026, a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, 52, a Mexican national, in Houston's Magnolia Park neighborhood. Salgado Araujo had been driving a work crew to a construction site when he was shot.

DHS subsequently acknowledged that Salgado Araujo was not the intended target of the operation — agents had approached him because his white van resembled one connected to their actual target. The officers involved in the shooting were not wearing body cameras, with DHS attributing the absence to government shutdowns that delayed equipment procurement.

  • ICE alleged Salgado Araujo "weaponized his vehicle" and tried to run over an officer, prompting the agent to fire in self-defense.
  • Three co-workers in the van denied that Salgado Araujo rammed ICE vehicles or endangered agents; one account indicated an agent ran toward the van from the side and fired through the passenger window.
  • Witnesses were detained by ICE following the shooting; federal judges subsequently ordered all three released.
  • The Harris County District Attorney opened a grand jury investigation; federal records reviewed by investigators revealed discrepancies between DHS's account and DPS intelligence records.

The Texas Tribune reported that ICE records attributed key intelligence about a white van to DPS — an account DPS disputes — raising further questions about the basis for the vehicle stop.
source: Texas Tribune / ABC News / Houston Public Media
